subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: does a seed need soil to germinate?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kya beej ko ankurit hone ke liye mitti chahiye?
answer: No; it needs water, air and warmth.

subject: science
prompt_en: Put the mosquito's stages in order: adult, egg, pupa, larva.
prompt_hi: Machhar ke stages sahi kram mein lagao: adult, anda, pupa, larva.
answer: Egg → larva → pupa → adult.

subject: science
prompt_en: Put the frog's stages in order: froglet, eggs, adult frog, tadpole.
prompt_hi: Medhak ke stages kram mein lagao: froglet, ande, adult medhak, tadpole.
answer: Eggs → tadpole → froglet → adult frog.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: after the rains, water collects in an old tyre and stays there for two weeks. What could you find in it?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: baarish ke baad ek purane tyre mein paani bhar gaya aur do hafte tak raha. Usme kya mil sakta hai?
answer: Mosquito larvae and pupae (wrigglers), and soon adult mosquitoes.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you see a tadpole that has tiny back legs. What will change next over the coming weeks?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek tadpole dikha jiske peechhe chhote pair nikal aaye hain. Agle kuch hafton mein aage kya badlega?
answer: Front legs will appear, the tail will shrink away and lungs will develop; it becomes a froglet and then a frog.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: a family empties and scrubs its cooler and flower-pot trays every week. What happens to the mosquito life cycle there?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek parivaar har hafte cooler aur gamlon ki trays khaali karke ragad ke saaf karta hai. Wahan machhar ke jeevan-chakra ka kya hoga?
answer: The eggs and larvae are thrown out before they can become adults (which takes about a week), so mosquitoes can't complete their life cycle there and there are fewer mosquitoes.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said the tadpole becomes a frog. Why does a tadpole have gills but a frog has lungs?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha tadpole medhak banta hai. Tadpole ke gills aur medhak ke lungs kyon hote hain?
answer: The tadpole lives only in water, so it breathes with gills; the adult frog lives on land and in water and breathes air with lungs (and through its moist skin).

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare a tadpole and an adult frog: where they live, how they breathe and how they move.
prompt_hi: Tadpole aur adult medhak compare karo: kahan rehte hain, kaise saans lete hain aur kaise chalte hain.
answer: Tadpole: lives in water, breathes with gills, swims with its tail. Adult frog: lives on land and in water, breathes with lungs (and its skin), jumps with strong back legs and swims with webbed feet.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why does the health department ask families to keep a weekly 'dry day' and empty all stored water containers?
prompt_hi: Swasthya vibhaag parivaaron se har hafte 'dry day' manaane aur saare jama paani ke bartan khaali karne ko kyon kehta hai?
answer: Mosquitoes lay eggs in still water, and the young take about a week to become adults; emptying containers weekly breaks the life cycle and reduces diseases like dengue and malaria.

subject: science
prompt_en: A farmer saves seeds from this year's best tomatoes to plant next year. Use the plant life cycle to explain why this works.
prompt_hi: Ek kisaan iss saal ke sabse achhe tamatar ke beej agle saal ke liye bacha ke rakhta hai. Paudhe ke jeevan-chakra se samjhao ye kyon kaam karta hai.
answer: The fruits contain seeds; next season the seeds germinate into seedlings, grow into plants, flower and make fruits again, so the cycle repeats.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw the mosquito life cycle as a circle with four stages. Mark which stages live in water.
prompt_hi: Machhar ka jeevan-chakra chaar stages wale circle mein banao. Kaunse stages paani mein rehte hain, mark karo.
answer: Egg → larva → pupa → adult → back to egg. The eggs are laid on the water, the larva and pupa live in the water, and the adult flies in the air.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu's notebook says: 'Frog life cycle: egg → frog. Tadpoles are tiny fish.' Fix it.
prompt_hi: Golu ki notebook mein likha hai: 'Medhak ka jeevan-chakra: anda → medhak. Tadpole chhoti machhliyan hain.' Ise theek karo.
answer: Egg → tadpole → tadpole with legs → froglet → frog; tadpoles are young frogs, not fish.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your neighbours how a mosquito grows and how they can stop mosquitoes breeding near their homes.
prompt_hi: Apne padosiyon ko samjhao ki machhar kaise badhta hai aur woh apne ghar ke paas machhar paidaa hone se kaise rok sakte hain.
answer: Key ideas: eggs are laid on still water → larvae → pupae (both in water) → adults in about a week; empty, scrub and cover water containers every week; don't let water collect in tyres, pots or coolers.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what is the big change in a frog's body during its life cycle called?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: medhak ke jeevan-chakra mein shareer ke bade badlaav ko kya kehte hain?
answer: Metamorphosis.

subject: science
prompt_en: Give one use each of sunlight, soil and water.
prompt_hi: Dhoop, mitti aur paani ka ek-ek upyog batao.
answer: Sunlight: plants make food; drying clothes and grain; solar power; light and warmth. Soil: growing crops; making bricks and pots. Water: drinking, farming, cleaning.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: a dry tissue is stuck inside the bottom of an 'empty' glass. The glass is pushed straight down, upside down, into a bucket of water. Will the tissue get wet?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek 'khaali' glass ke tale mein sookha tissue chipka hai. Glass ko ulta karke seedha baalti ke paani mein dabaya. Kya tissue geela hoga?
answer: No, it stays dry; the air inside the glass takes up space and keeps the water out.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: on a simple balance (a light stick hung by a thread from its middle), you hang two identical big balloons, one blown up and one empty, so the stick balances first with both empty. Which side goes down when one is blown up?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek saade taraazu pe (beech se dhaage pe latki halki lakdi), do ek jaise bade gubbare latkao. Pehle dono khaali gubbaron ke saath lakdi barabar karo, phir ek ko phula do. Kaunsi taraf jhukegi?
answer: The side with the blown-up balloon dips a little; the air pushed into it has weight. The difference is small, so a light stick and big balloons help you see it.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: a village cuts down all the forest on a hillside. What may happen to the soil there in the next monsoon?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek gaon pahaadi dhalaan ka poora jungle kaat deta hai. Agle monsoon mein wahan ki mitti ka kya ho sakta hai?
answer: Rain will wash the soil away (soil erosion), because there are no roots to hold it; landslides become more likely.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said the tissue stays dry. Why couldn't the water get in?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha tissue sookha rehta hai. Paani andar kyon nahi ja paaya?
answer: The glass was full of air; air takes up space, and with nowhere to escape it kept the water out.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare air and a bottle of packaged drinking water. You pay for one but not the other. Are both resources? Why?
prompt_hi: Hawa aur packed peene ke paani ki botal compare karo. Ek ke paise dete ho, doosre ke nahi. Kya dono sansaadhan hain? Kyon?
answer: Yes, both: a resource is anything useful from nature, whether we pay for it or not, and we can't live without air even for minutes.

subject: science
prompt_en: Name three things a farmer uses from nature to grow rice.
prompt_hi: 3 cheezein batao jo kisaan chawal ugane ke liye prakriti se leta hai.
answer: Any three: soil, water (rain, rivers, groundwater), sunlight, air (and seeds).

subject: science
prompt_en: In many villages of Odisha and Jharkhand, families collect sal leaves, mahua flowers and kendu (tendu) leaves from forests. How do these help them, and why should forests be used carefully?
prompt_hi: Odisha aur Jharkhand ke kai gaon mein parivaar jungle se sal ke patte, mahua ke phool aur kendu (tendu) patte ikattha karte hain. Isse unki kya madad hoti hai, aur jungle ko soch-samajh ke kyon use karna chahiye?
answer: Sal leaves make plates and bring income; mahua flowers give food and oil; kendu leaves are sold for income; forests also give firewood and medicines. If people cut or take too much, the forest can't regrow, so they should take only what can grow back.

subject: science
prompt_en: Make a web diagram with 'Forest' in the middle and at least five arrows pointing to things it gives us.
prompt_hi: Ek web diagram banao, beech mein 'Jungle', aur kam se kam paanch teer un cheezon ki taraf jo woh hume deta hai.
answer: Any five: wood, fruits, honey, medicines, leaves, a home for animals, clean air, holding the soil, helping bring rain.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Air isn't a resource; it's free and everywhere, so it doesn't matter if factories make it dirty.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Hawa sansaadhan nahi hai; ye muft hai aur har jagah hai, isliye factory use ganda kare toh farak nahi padta.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Air is a vital resource; polluted air harms the breathing and health of people, animals and plants. Being free doesn't make it unimportant.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child that air is 'something', not 'nothing', with one experiment.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko ek experiment ke saath samjhao ki hawa 'kuch' hai, 'kuch nahi' nahi.
answer: Key ideas: air takes up space (an upside-down glass keeps a tissue dry under water); air has weight (the balloon balance tips); we feel air as wind.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: why is soil called a precious resource?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: mitti ko keemti sansaadhan kyon kehte hain?
answer: Plants grow in it and get water and minerals from it; it takes hundreds of years to form but can be washed away quickly.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why is coal called non-renewable?
prompt_hi: Koyle ko non-renewable kyon kehte hain?
answer: It took millions of years to form from buried plants, and we use it far faster than it can form, so it will run out.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: a town pumps out lots of groundwater every day for years, more than the rain soaks back into the ground. What happens to the water level in its wells?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek shehar saalon tak roz bahut zameen ka paani nikaalta hai, jitna baarish wapas zameen mein jaati hai usse zyada. Uske kuon mein paani ke star ka kya hoga?
answer: It keeps falling, and wells and borewells may dry up.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: one car runs on petrol and another is an electric car charged with solar panels. After ten years of running, which one has been using up a non-renewable resource?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek car petrol se chalti hai aur doosri electric car solar panel se charge hoti hai. Das saal chalne ke baad, kaunsi car non-renewable sansaadhan khatam kar rahi thi?
answer: The petrol car, because petroleum is non-renewable; the solar-charged car runs on renewable sunlight.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said wells can dry up even though it rains. Why doesn't the rain keep them full?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha baarish ke baad bhi kuen sookh sakte hain. Baarish unhe bhara kyon nahi rakhti?
answer: Rain refills groundwater only slowly and partly (much of it runs off, especially from concrete); if we pump faster than it refills, the level falls.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare sunlight and petrol as sources of energy.
prompt_hi: Urja ke source ke roop mein dhoop aur petrol compare karo.
answer: Sunlight is renewable, free, clean and comes back every day; petrol is non-renewable, limited and pollutes the air when burned.

subject: science
prompt_en: Give three ways your family can save water at home.
prompt_hi: 3 tareeke batao jinse tumhara parivaar ghar pe paani bacha sakta hai.
answer: Any three: turn off the tap while brushing; take a bucket bath instead of a long shower; fix leaking taps; reuse water from washing vegetables or RO waste water for plants or cleaning; collect rainwater.

subject: science
prompt_en: There is so much water on Earth. Why can't we just use sea water for our homes and farms?
prompt_hi: Dharti pe itna paani hai. Hum ghar aur kheton ke liye samundar ka paani hi kyon nahi use kar sakte?
answer: About 97% of Earth's water is salty sea water, which is unfit for drinking and for most crops, and removing the salt takes a lot of energy; of the small amount of fresh water, most is frozen, so very little is easy to use.

subject: science
prompt_en: Imagine all of Earth's water filled a bucket of 100 mugs. Draw it and show about how many mugs are fresh water, and how many of those are frozen.
prompt_hi: Socho Dharti ka saara paani 100 mug wali ek baalti mein hai. Drawing banao aur dikhao ki lagbhag kitne mug meetha paani hai, aur unme se kitne jame hue hain.
answer: About 3 mugs are fresh water, and about 2 of those are frozen as ice; the remaining roughly 1 mug is mostly underground, with only a tiny bit in rivers and lakes.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Trees are renewable, so we can cut down the whole forest; it will grow back next year.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Ped renewable hain, isliye poora jungle kaat sakte hain; agle saal wapas ug jaayega.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Trees take many years, even decades, to grow; cutting faster than they regrow destroys the forest and the animals' homes. A forest stays renewable only if it is used carefully and replanted.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your family the difference between renewable and non-renewable resources, and two habits that help.
prompt_hi: Apne parivaar ko renewable aur non-renewable sansaadhanon ka farak samjhao, aur do aadatein jo madad karti hain.
answer: Key ideas: renewable resources are replaced by nature quickly (sun, wind, water) but can still be overused; non-renewable ones formed over millions of years and are limited (coal, petrol, gas); habits: switch off lights and fans, walk, cycle or use public transport, save water, use solar power.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: name one renewable and one non-renewable source of energy.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: urja ka ek renewable aur ek non-renewable source batao.
answer: Renewable: sunlight, wind or flowing water. Non-renewable: coal, petroleum or natural gas.

subject: science
prompt_en: What is a constellation? Name two.
prompt_hi: Taaramandal (constellation) kya hota hai? Do naam batao.
answer: A group of stars that forms a pattern as seen from Earth. Examples: Saptarishi (Ursa Major or Big Dipper), Orion (Mriga), Cassiopeia, Leo.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: how does a big street lamp look from 5 km away at night, compared with from 50 metres? What does this tell you about stars?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: raat mein ek badi street light 5 km door se kaisi dikhegi, 50 metre ke mukaable? Isse taaron ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
answer: From far away it looks like a tiny point of light; stars look tiny because they are very far away, even though they are huge.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: on a winter night at 8 pm you see Orion low in the eastern sky. Where will it be around midnight?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: sardi ki raat 8 baje tumhe Orion poorab ke aasmaan mein neeche dikhta hai. Aadhi raat ke aaspaas woh kahan hoga?
answer: Higher up in the sky, having moved westward; stars rise in the east and set in the west, like the Sun.
